sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.content: EU formally classified China as 'systemic rival' in June 2023. South Korea-China diplomatic tensions over ambassador remarks. Chinese executive detained at Munich Airport. Ukraine counteroffensive in early stages. Japan Nikkei at 33-year highs. None were primary US equity movers.

sections.title: Commodities
sections.content: WTI crude soft near $67-68, reflecting demand concerns and CPI energy deflation. Gold ~$1,945-1,960, supported by pause expectations but capped by resilient dollar. PBoC rate cut signals deeper China weakness. Copper under pressure at ~$3.78/lb.

recommendations.thesis: AI momentum leader continuing post-earnings surge. Closed June 13 at $40.99 (+3.9%), firmly in an uptrend. FOMC pause at 2:00 PM is a direct tailwind for growth/tech names. NVDA is the consensus AI infrastructure play with no sign of momentum exhaustion. Entry on a pullback toward $41.20 (near prior day close), targeting $43.00 (round number + measured move). Stop at June 13 low of $40.07 respects intraday support.
recommendations.catalyst: FOMC rate pause announcement 2:00 PM ET; continued AI capex cycle narrative
recommendations.risk: Hawkish dot plot revision to 5.6% year-end rate could trigger growth selloff. Extended run-up leaves room for sharp reversal on any negative surprise. Consider taking half-profits before 2:00 PM FOMC.

recommendations.thesis: Oversold bounce after a dramatic -5.9% selloff on June 13 (opened $132.32, closed $124.53) while the broad market rallied. This was rotation/profit-taking, not fundamental deterioration — AMD remains a key AI/MI300 beneficiary. The selloff created a gap that dip buyers will target. FOMC pause supports semiconductor sector broadly. Entry near $125.50 (above prior close to confirm buying interest), target $128.50 (partial gap fill), stop $122.00 (below round number support).
recommendations.catalyst: Mean reversion from oversold June 13 selloff; FOMC pause supportive for semis; AI/MI300 narrative intact
recommendations.risk: If hawkish dots trigger broad growth selloff, AMD as high-beta could continue lower. The June 13 selloff may reflect something stock-specific. Volume and opening action critical to confirm the bounce.

recommendations.thesis: Post-earnings dip-buy after sell-the-news reversal. ORCL reported strong Q4 FY23 on June 12 (revenue $13.8B +17% YoY, cloud +23%, full-year revenue hit record $50B). Stock gapped up to $120 on June 13 but reversed hard to close at $113.01 (-5.4%). The earnings were genuinely strong — the selloff was an overreaction. Dip buyers should re-engage on June 14. Entry around $117.50 (expecting gap-up open toward prior day's midrange), target $119.50 (approaching the June 13 open level), stop $115.00.
recommendations.catalyst: Dip-buying into objectively strong earnings; cloud growth narrative intact; FOMC pause supports tech
recommendations.risk: June 13 reversal from $120 to $113 shows heavy overhead supply. If market turns risk-off on hawkish FOMC, ORCL could retest $113 lows. Overhead resistance significant.

recommendations.thesis: Mean reversion short after record 13-consecutive-day winning streak. TSLA closed June 13 at $258.71 — its longest-ever streak. Market cap added $240B over the run. Stock more than doubled YTD (+108%). Short sellers already lost $7B. Statistical probability of a 14th consecutive up day is very low. Exhaustion signals building. Entry on any early-session strength toward $260 (above prior close), targeting $254 (support from prior week), tight stop at $263 (above June 13 high of $259.19).
recommendations.catalyst: Streak exhaustion; FOMC hawkish dot plot risk could trigger rotation out of high-beta; mean reversion probability
recommendations.risk: Momentum can persist irrationally. If FOMC is dovish, TSLA could squeeze higher. Ford/GM NACS adoption catalysts still fresh. Tight stop limits downside to ~1.2%.

recommendations.thesis: Steady AI/Copilot beneficiary grinding higher. MSFT is the highest-quality mega-cap AI play — enterprise Copilot narrative, Azure cloud growth, OpenAI partnership. Less volatile than pure-play semis. FOMC pause directly supports growth. Entry near $329 (between prior close and expected open), target $333 (continuation toward round number). Lower conviction due to modest R:R in a single session.
recommendations.catalyst: FOMC pause; AI/Copilot enterprise demand; flight to quality within tech
recommendations.risk: Limited single-day upside. Already near highs. R:R marginal for a day trade. Best as a smaller position or swing hold.
